title: Weight bound for retained candidates
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0<\tau\leq 1$ be rational, let an estimate assign a rational number to every finite coordinate set $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and every finite subset of $J$, and let the estimate differ from the true restricted Fourier weight of a Boolean target function by less than $\tau^2/4$ at every such pair. Let $k<n$, let $A$ be a finite family of subsets of the coordinates, and let $S$ belong to the retained family obtained from the candidates $U$ and $U\cup\{k\}$ for $U\in A$ by keeping those whose estimate on the first $k+1$ coordinates, restricted to their part in that prefix, exceeds $\tau^2/2$. Then the true restricted Fourier weight on that prefix at the free part of $S$ is strictly greater than $\tau^2/4$.
hypotheses_covered: global accuracy error strictly less than τ²/4
natural number k with k < n
finite active family of coordinate subsets
S belongs to the retained family
